channel.title: The Western Producer - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Western Producer (producer.com)

item.title: Richardson back in the fold at canola council
item.description: Richardson International has rejoined the Canola Council of Canada after a nearly nine-year hiatus.

item.title: Saskatchewan firm wants its camera system to go global
item.description: A Saskatchewan tech startup is one of the 15 agtech companies from across Canada and the United Kingdom to join Cohort 5 of Cultivator powered by Conexus’s AgTech Accelerator.

item.title: Bank of Canada holds rates, says it would hike them to prevent persistent inflation
item.description: The Bank of Canada on Wednesday kept its key policy rate on hold as widely expected but Governor Tiff Macklem said the central bank was ready to raise rates to prevent higher energy prices becoming persistent inflation.

item.title: Crop merchant Louis Dreyfus reports lower profits, higher volumes for 2025
item.description: Global agricultural commodity merchant Louis Dreyfus Company said on Wednesday it had recorded a decline in annual profit, driven by lower prices for most crops and market uncertainty arising from tariffs and economic concerns.

item.title: Research recruits beneficial bacteria against Strep suis in piglets
item.description: Calgary researchers hope to engineer beneficial bacteria as an enzyme delivery system to fight Strep suis bacterial infections in piglets.

item.title: Out-of-season elk tags offered to control damage
item.description: The elk depredation program recently announced in Saskatchewan isn’t likely to help producers dealing with damage, says a wildlife expert.

item.title: Saskatchewan offers exemption to federal gun buyback
item.description: Saskatchewan is exempting firearm owners from the most recent federal gun ban and buyback program.

item.title: Saskatchewan agriculture spending to rise next fiscal year
item.description: Saskatchewan’s agricultural spending is going up next year on the expectation of higher AgriStability claims.

item.title: Federal government funds Quebec organic fertilizer company
item.description: Québec-based Solugen, which makes organic nitrogen fertilizer from hog manure, has recieved $20 million in federal funding.

item.title: Proposed Sask. poultry research facility gets funding influx
item.description: A recently-funded poultry facility at the University of Saskatchewan will allow researchers to work on poultry barn lighting, housing and feed systems.
